A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a complete characterization of the set of wealth processes adapted to the finer filtrations that are implementable in a dynamically effectively market, and show how this set of implementable wealth processes can be used to characterize the set of Pareto optimal consumption processes.

we have shown that the existence of contingent claims on aggregateconsumption and the market portfolio is sufficient to implement Pareto optimal allocations, even in the presence of short- or long-term risks and personal risks.
we provide sufficient conditions for a dynamically effectively complete consumption market to exist.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the existence of dynamically effective markets for contingent claims is sufficient for the existence of a Pareto optimal allocation.
the CCAPM is not only a model of consumption-based pricing, but also a model of consumption allocation.
in order to achieve Pareto optimal consumption, a sufficiently varied asset set must exist.
